question.text: A plot of In \(\mathrm{k}\) against \(\frac{1}{\mathrm{~T}}\) (abscissa) is expected to be a straight line with intercept on ordinate axis equal to

solution.text:
Hints: \(\Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ}=-\mathrm{RT} \operatorname{InK}\) or, \(\Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ}-\mathrm{T} \Delta \mathrm{S}^{\circ}=-\mathrm{RT} \operatorname{InK}\)
or, \(\operatorname{InK}=\frac{-\Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ}}{\mathrm{RT}}+\frac{\Delta \mathrm{S}^{\circ}}{\mathrm{R}}\) comparing with \(\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{m} \cdot \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{c}\) \(\therefore \mathrm{y}\) intercept is \(\frac{\Delta \mathrm{S}^{\circ}}{\mathrm{R}}\)
